name: Azrikam
overview: Azrikam was a male member of the tribe of Levi, specifically connected to the Merarite clan, descendants of Merari son of Levi. He is uniquely identified as the son of Hashabiah, situating him within the Levitical lineage responsible for temple duties. His mention in 1 Chronicles 9:14 highlights his role within the priestly or Levitical community during the post-exilic period.
namesAndTitles: The name Azrikam means '[my] help arises,' reflecting a reliance on divine assistance. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 9:14, does not appear to be given directly by God but carries a meaningful Hebrew significance consistent with Levitical heritage.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Azrikam as the son of Hashabiah, with an inferred relationship to Hasshub as his father. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical text concerning Azrikam.
scriptureSignificance: Azrikam's significance lies in his role within the Levitical priesthood, particularly among the Merarites, who were entrusted with specific temple responsibilities. His mention in 1 Chronicles 9:14 situates him within the restored community of Israel, emphasizing the continuity of Levitical service and the faithful preservation of worship practices after the exile.
